confidence_reason: Current source and a complete ordinary-key browser route establish the long dependency chain and safe geometry; only selected recovery scenarios were exercised.

confirmed: The WAIT FOR BOTH rider clutch, A/B decks, cargo x2 pad, opposite exits, and cross-arrival gates are real.
Both heroes and two cargo stages contribute to a demonstrated clear.
missed_mechanics: The deck direction follows unequal total load only when each side has a hero rider.
Pac plus one light sac, rather than two sacs, supplies the x2 lower cargo pad and releases the right return sac.
DELIVERY and RETURN are persistent partner-opening exit latches.
incorrect_inferences: The first pass counted visible shaft gaps as hazard exposure, but source has no hazards and provides bases and recovery stops.
The first pass scored several earlier lift, lane, and cargo devices as wholly new; the new concept is the coupled rider-and-load rule and its return-trip transfer.
changed_judgments: Hazards fall from 2 to 0 because shaft geometry catches misses and no lethal zone is authored.
Novelty falls from 4 to 3 because lift, split-lane, cargo plate, and latch ideas were already introduced; the counterweight rule is the new transfer.
Execution rises from 2 to 3 after the demonstrated route requires unloading, reboarding, a second cargo move, and endpoint jumps.

Timing changes from unknown to 1 because rider-gated motion and safe stops allow deliberate setup; recovery changes from unknown to 2 because mistakes can require another deck traversal without an authored death reset.
unresolved: The full range of recoveries from every possible cargo placement and first-time human comprehension of the display remain unmeasured.

single_operator_note: One operator must alternate both key sets while tracking deck riders, two sacs, and load reversal. That divided attention is outside the two-human baseline scores.
